pr.title: gh-89687: fix `get_type_hints` with dataclasses `__init__` generation
pr.body:
This is a rather brave idea to manipulate `globals`, but it looks like it works.
It can backfire is some corner cases, though. But, I am not able to think about any. Ideas? 🙂 

<!-- issue-number: [bpo-45524](https://bugs.python.org/issue45524) -->
https://bugs.python.org/issue45524
<!-- /issue-number -->


CC @AlexWaygood @aidan.b.clark

<!-- gh-issue-number: gh-89687 -->
* Issue: gh-89687
<!-- /gh-issue-number -->

@@ -1014,6 +1014,18 @@ def _process_class(cls, init, repr, eq, order, unsafe_hash, frozen,
     if init:
         # Does this class have a post-init function?
         has_post_init = hasattr(cls, _POST_INIT_NAME)
+        init_globals = globals
+        if has_dataclass_bases:
+            # If dataclass has other dataclass as a base type,
+            # it might have existing `__init__` method.
+            # We need to change its `globals`, because otherwise
+            # we might end up with unsolvable annotations. For example:
+            # `def __init__(self, d: collections.OrderedDict) -> None:`
+            # won't be able to resolve `collections.OrderedDict`
+            # with wrong `globals`, when placed in different modules. #45524
+            super_init = getattr(cls, '__init__', None)
+            if super_init is not None:
+                init_globals = getattr(super_init, '__globals__', globals)
review_comments.body:
I am a little queasy about tinkering with `globals()` directly like this (though I can't point to any tests failing at all!). 

Perhaps we could make sure that `init_globals` is always a different dictionary to `globals()`, rather than being sometimes-a-different-dict-and-sometimes-actually-globals-itself? The following seems to pass tests just as well:

```suggestion
        init_globals = dict(globals)
        if has_dataclass_bases:
            # If dataclass has other dataclass as a base type,
            # it might have existing `__init__` method.
            # We need to change its `globals`, because otherwise
            # we might end up with unsolvable annotations. For example:
            # `def __init__(self, d: collections.OrderedDict) -> None:`
            # won't be able to resolve `collections.OrderedDict`
            # with wrong `globals`, when placed in different modules. #45524
            super_init = getattr(cls, '__init__', None)
            if super_init is not None:
                init_globals = getattr(super_init, '__globals__', init_globals )
```

review_comments.body: Bikeshedding point, but: would it be better to put these tests in `test_dataclasses`? For the similar issue with `TypedDict`, the new tests were put next to the other `TypedDict` tests. Moreover, given that this is a *very* specific issue with the way that the `dataclasses` module generates `__init__` functions, it seems like more of a `dataclasses` bug than a `get_type_hints` bug.

issue_comments.body:
I found a corner case: when I define a proxy module, say `dataclass_textanno2.py`, with this content:

```python
from __future__ import annotations

import dataclasses
from test import dataclass_textanno  # We need to be sure that `Foo` is not in scope


class Custom:
    pass


@dataclasses.dataclass
class Child(dataclass_textanno.Bar):
    custom: Custom


@dataclasses.dataclass(init=False)
class WithFutureInit(Child):
    def __init__(self, foo: dataclass_textanno.Foo, custom: Custom) -> None:
        pass
```
